CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness and tingling in bilateral hands.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
60-year-old right-handed male referred for evaluation of numbness and tingling in both hands for several weeks. Symptoms began after a motor vehicle accident in December with bilateral wrist fractures. Right wrist injury was more severe than left. Since the fractures healed, patient has noticed increased tingling and numbness, which has worsened significantly over the past month. On the right side, symptoms extend from the middle and ring fingers up the forearm. On the left side, symptoms extend from the pinky and ring finger. Patient reports the symptoms are primarily soreness with occasional throbbing and associated weakness, particularly with hand use. Tingling is more prominent when painful but becomes dull when pain subsides. Symptoms occur mainly at night but come and go throughout the day. Patient denies loss of sensation but notes decreased sensitivity overall. Patient also reports mild neck stiffness since hitting his head during the accident, which was noted as a contusion. Patient wears splints on both wrists, with right wrist splint providing more relief. Has been prescribed nerve pain medication but has not been taking it consistently. Car wreck weekend was difficult.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: fatigue and weight gain. Eyes: floaters. Cardiovascular: shortness of breath and leg swelling. Gastrointestinal: excessive appetite and bloating. Endocrine: increased hunger. Skin: nail bed changes, dryness, and itching. Musculoskeletal: gout and muscle pain. Remainder of review of systems: negative.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Prediabetes (controlled with diet modification)
Hypertension
Anxiety
Status post bilateral wrist fractures (December, healed)
Status post head contusion (December)

MEDICATIONS
Coreg (for hypertension)
Lexapro (for anxiety)
Nerve pain medication (prescribed but not taking consistently)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Right-handed. Motor vehicle accident in December with bilateral wrist injuries.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurologic examination: Pin prick sensation diminished in third and fourth fingers on the right hand; sensation decreased in fourth and fifth fingers on the left hand. Reflexes 1+ and symmetric in upper extremities; 2+ at knees; toes downgoing bilaterally. Tinel sign positive at both wrists and both elbows. Rest of examination normal.

RESULTS
Neurologic examination as documented above.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome (suspected). Clinical presentation most consistent with bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome related to previous wrist trauma.

Plan:
1. Schedule EMG (electromyography) test to determine exact location of nerve irritation and pinpoint areas of nerve issues.
2. Patient to continue wearing wrist splints on both sides.
3. Follow-up visit after EMG results.
4. If symptoms persist after testing, consider referral to hand clinic for possible injections or carpal tunnel release surgery, or referral to orthopedist for similar treatment options.
